sources.citation: Pache, Matthias J. 2018. Contributions to Chibchan historical linguistics. PhD dissertation, Universiteit Leiden. Sec. 2.3.11 'Duit', pp. 355–357; 2.3.11.1.1 'Duit vowels and suprasegmentals', pp. 355–356.
sources.note: Silent on Duit stress: the subsection headed 'Duit vowels and suprasegmentals' only tabulates the five vowel graphemes from Uricoechea and notes possible non-syllabic allophones of i/u; p. 355 states 'The only data on this language are available from Uricoechea's 1871 work'. (For the sister language Muisca, pp. 431–432: 'There are no indications that tone, stress, or vowel nasality were contrastive in Muisca … In Lugo's work, stress is mostly (in approximately 70 to 80% of the cases) indicated on the last syllable of a word', citing Constenla Umaña 1984b: 103–6 — Muisca, not Duit.)

sources.citation: Chevrier, Natacha. 2017. Analyse de la phonologie du bribri (chibcha) dans une perspective typologique. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lyon 2. Annex sec. 1.4 'Muisca et duit : consonne labio-vélaire', p. ~412.
sources.note: Nothing on Duit accent; states Muisca and Duit have not been spoken since the 18th century, descriptions rest on colonial documents and 'aucune donnée phonétique n'est disponible' (regarding the labial-velar).

sources.citation: Uricoechea, Ezequiel. 1871. Gramática, vocabulario, catecismo i confesionario de la lengua chibcha según antiguos manuscritos anónimos e inéditos. (Collection linguistique américaine 1.) Paris: Maisonneuve. Introducción pp. xl–xlii: Duit catechism specimen with Spanish and Muisca parallels and a glossary footnote.
sources.note: Nothing. The sole primary attestation of Duit is a two-page written specimen; a few acute accents appear in the transcription (Tótia 'Hijo', Uequéneca '¿de qué modo?', chí 'ser') without any comment on accent or pronunciation.
Nothing on stress; both state the Uricoechea 1871 catechism fragment is the only known document; es cites Adelaar & Muysken 2004 and Constenla Umaña 1995 (Boletín Museo del Oro 38-39).
